resolved_items.primary_evidence: The paper's fixed nonzero roundoffs cannot be embedded as a constant Lean family because D016 requires both roundoffs to tend to zero. Conversely, the paper does not cover the arbitrary non-MGS certificate-bearing families admitted by D027/D037.

resolved_items.resolution: D027 is an abstract per-restart certificate type. It packages a key dimension, basis and perturbation data, least-squares and rank conditions, bounded contraction factors, and correction-level error estimates; it is not an implementation predicate for fully stored MGS-Arnoldi.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: The complete P16LowPrecisionMGSRestart declaration exposes all fields through constructor D037. PDF page 40 explicitly requires a Krylov basis computed by MGS Arnoldi and fully formed and stored.

resolved_items.resolution: D037 directly assumes backward_correction_bound and forward_correction_bound together with bounds on backwardFactor and forwardFactor. It does not enforce MGS orthogonalization, first-key minimality, or derivation of the modular accuracy parameters from low-precision operations.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: D037's final fields contain the two correction inequalities and factor bounds. By contrast, PDF pages 27-29 derive the key iteration and modular bounds from MGS, and PDF page 41 invokes that derivation to obtain equation (6.21) and the contraction factors.

resolved_items.resolution: S02 fails. Although the finite real system and outer index match, Lean adds an arbitrary filter parameter, t-dependent executions and roundoffs, and a key dimension fixed across t for each restart.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: Theorem 6.3 uses fixed uhigh and ulow and obtains a possibly restart-dependent k_i. D016 has uHigh, uLow and xHat as functions of t, while each D027 certificate selects keyDimension outside its t-indexed fields.

resolved_items.resolution: S04 fails. The record includes several paper assumptions but adds asymptotic precision hypotheses, weakens the approximate iterate equality to one-sided bounds, and assumes aggregate high-roundoff and correction estimates that the paper derives.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: PDF page 17 assumes ||xHat_i|| lesssim ||xHat_(i+1)|| approximately ||x||. D016 records current-to-next and next-to-solution upper bounds only, plus backward_high_roundoff_bound and forward_high_roundoff_bound; D037 supplies the correction bounds.

resolved_items.resolution: S06 fails rather than remaining unclear. The complete dependencies are understood, but p16MuchLessThanOneAt and the polynomial representation do not preserve the paper's conventions exactly.

resolved_items.resolution: S08 fails. The declaration specifies an abstract certified correction solve, not execution by unpreconditioned fully stored MGS-GMRES.

resolved_items.resolution: S11 fails. The visible high-precision residual, update, and residual-cast models are compatible with the paper, but the complete low-precision certificate does not tie epsilonC, epsilonLS, or epsilonX to low-precision MGS operations.

D037 merely requires its accuracy functions to be nonnegative and tend to zero, and replaces condition (3.3)'s columnwise perturbation bound with separate RHS and Frobenius matrix bounds.

resolved_items.resolution: S14 passes in isolation. An additive remainder that is Big-O of (uHigh+uLow)^2 is a defensible rigorous interpretation of inequalities that discard negligible second-order terms, although the paper does not uniquely prescribe this filter formulation.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: PDF page 4 explicitly states that its comparison symbols drop negligible second-order terms. D008/D024 make that convention explicit through an O(scale^2) remainder.

resolved_items.resolution: S15 fails. The finite-dimensional real setting is preserved, but replacing fixed-precision executions by arbitrary filter-indexed families is not merely a scalar-field or dimension specialization and materially restricts applicability.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: Theorem 6.3 is stated for fixed unit roundoffs. D016 requires uHigh and uLow to converge to zero and requires one certificate whose key dimension works across every t.

resolved_items.resolution: The declaration is not logically empty, but S16 fails the intended-reason check. Exact positive-dimensional identity-system families can satisfy the records, while the difficult MGS contraction properties are already constructor hypotheses.
resolved_items.primary_evidence: D016 permits positive-dimensional exact systems, and D037 permits keyDimension=n, zero perturbations, zero factors, and exact correction inequalities. PDF pages 27-29 and 40-41 instead derive the key-dimension and contraction properties from MGS analysis.

lean_implies_paper.reasoning: Lean proves per-index eventual recurrences only for filter-indexed runs already carrying abstract correction certificates. It does not establish that a fixed nonzero-precision fully stored MGS-GMRES execution supplies such a run, nor does it give one fixed precision at which every restart recurrence and attainable-floor conclusion hold.

paper_implies_lean.reasoning: The paper's fixed-precision theorem does not establish the declaration's arbitrary-filter family statement, a t-uniform key dimension, exact shared P(n,n), or explicit per-index Big-O witnesses. It also does not assert the result for abstract certificate-bearing runs unrelated to MGS generation.

remaining_uncertainties: The paper does not uniquely formalize its discarded second-order terms, so the precise joint Big-O scale and filter semantics are not determined by the source.
Theorem 6.3 suppresses the restart dependence of c(n,k_i), so the exact intended uniformization over varying key dimensions is not explicit.

findings.evidence: PDF pages 27-29 derive the MGS key iteration and modular bounds, and PDF pages 40-41 use them to bound both contraction factors. D037 neither requires MGS generation nor proves these properties; it assumes the bounded factors and both correction-level contraction inequalities.
findings.impact: The declaration states an abstract certificate-composition result rather than Theorem 6.3 for the specified algorithm.

findings.evidence: The paper applies at every restart of one execution with fixed uhigh and ulow. Lean uses t-dependent precisions tending to zero and has forall i outside a separately existential and eventual first-order inequality.
findings.impact: No single fixed nonzero precision parameter is guaranteed to satisfy all restart recurrences, so repeated geometric contraction to the stated floors cannot be recovered.

findings.evidence: Paper condition (3.3) is columnwise, and Section 6.3 requires all correction operations to be low-precision MGS-GMRES. D037 uses separate RHS and aggregate Frobenius perturbation bounds and leaves its accuracy functions unconnected to uLow operation models.
findings.impact: The formal certificate does not preserve the selected algorithm's modular floating-point hypotheses.

findings.evidence: The paper uses unspecified low-degree c(n,k_i). Lean uses one nonnegative-coefficient polynomial evaluated at P(n,n), with no degree bound and with keyDimension fixed across t.
findings.impact: The inner-dimension dependence and low-degree worst-case constant convention are materially changed.

findings.evidence: The paper explicitly discards negligible second-order terms, while D008/D024 represent them by additive O((uHigh+uLow)^2) remainders.
findings.impact: This choice is reasonable in isolation and is not a basis for rejection, but its exact filter semantics are stronger and more specific than the paper states.

rationale: The declaration correctly represents the finite real system, exact and computed quantities, Euclidean and Frobenius norms, backward and forward error definitions, useful contraction inequality direction, and first-order floor scales. The complete dossier nevertheless shows that it replaces the fixed-precision fully stored MGS-GMRES theorem with a nonuniform asymptotic statement over abstract runs whose crucial correction contractions are already assumptions. Because actual paper executions are not supplied by the Lean proposition and the paper does not cover all Lean certificate families, neither implication holds.
